transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sarah Conway (Acme Head of ML), Omar Haddad (Acme Infra Lead), Priya Shah (Acme Security), Kenji Tanaka (Acme PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Short decision sprint kickoff. Primary ask: choose hosting mode for pilot (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with clear acceptance criteria and benchmark plan.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Alright everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro and then jump into the decision sprint goals. Um, Sarah can you give us a 60‑second on the business driver?
[00:14] Sarah Conway: Yeah, sure. We want an internal "doc‑assistant" for manufacturing QA — the core need is high recall on spec questions and safe withholding of PII. Timeline is tight, we want a pilot within three weeks ideally to demo to ops.
[00:31] Omar Haddad: From infra, our main constraints are: network egress rules, internal KMS for keys, and we limit external data retention. So private hosting is attractive but we also care about time to market.
[00:46] Arjun Patel: Got it. For the pilot we usually run a two‑step: baseline qualit eval on hosted, then a throughput/latency bench on both hosted and dedicated. That lets you compare cost per token and p99 latency tradeoffs.
[01:02] Priya Shah: Quick Q — do Redwood hosted endpoints support customer‑managed keys or at least bring‑your‑own KMS? That's a blocker for us unless we can isolate keys.
[01:14] Diego Ruiz: Short answer: hosted supports envelope encryption and we can integrate with some customer KMS flows, but private/dedicated gives you full control and auditability. I'll caveat: some KMS/HSM flows require additional compliance review.
[01:28] Kenji Tanaka: And what about autoscaling? We need bursts for end‑of‑shift reports — can Dedicated handle quick bursts without cold starts?
[01:40] Arjun Patel: Yes, dedicated pools are configured with burst capacity; the SLO for cold starts is much better than spinning up new private nodes. However dedicated is more predictable in throughput but needs reserved capacity. Hosted is elastic but you pay higher unit cost at scale.
[01:56] Maya Chen: Let's anchor success criteria — what do you need to see to call the pilot a win?
[02:03] Sarah Conway: Three things: 1) p99 latency under 800ms for 512‑token prompts in production‑like load, 2) accuracy on our eval prompts: F1 > 0.82 on QA set, and 3) security controls — keys and audit logs aligned with our internal compliance.
[02:21] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll make the bench tests target those.
[02:26] [02:26] Speaker 1: (background) And also cost target?
[02:29] Sarah Conway: We want monthly run cost under $6k for pilot traffic, but flexible if accuracy/SLA demands more.
[02:36] Arjun Patel: Noted. For workload sizing, can you walk us through typical concurrency and token distribution?
[02:43] Omar Haddad: Typical shift: 120 concurrent agents at peak, average prompt length 180 tokens, average response 420 tokens. So long tail exists — occasional 4k token documents during batch processing.
[03:02] Arjun Patel: That's helpful. We'll simulate that in the benchmark — mixed distribution with a 2% tail at 4k tokens. We'll measure tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and p95/p99 latencies.
[03:16] Diego Ruiz: Quick note — KV cache behavior matters for your workload because many prompts will reuse prefixes (templates). If we can cache prefixes, Dedicated and Private will show better token throughput. Hosted supports prefix caching too but persistence differs.
[03:33] Priya Shah: About data residency; some documents cannot leave EU region. Would Redwood hosted offer EU‑only endpoints?
[03:40] Maya Chen: Yes we have region options; for hosted we can pin to EU region. Dedicated can also be deployed in region of choice, private obviously stays where you put it.
[03:49] Kenji Tanaka: For the benchmark plan, what samples do you need from us?
[03:52] Arjun Patel: 50 sample docs representative of the tokens and 10 canonical prompts. Also a small eval set (200 labeled Q/A pairs) for quality regression tests.
[04:01] Sarah Conway: We can assemble that by end of week.
[04:04] [04:04] Speaker 2: (crosstalk, phone)
[04:07] Maya Chen: I'll also highlight decision criteria we've seen work: if security/compliance is top priority, lean private; if time to market and lower operational burden matter, hosted; if you need predictable cost and throughput, dedicated. But we can also run a hybrid path — start hosted for eval, then migrate to dedicated.
[04:24] Omar Haddad: The hybrid path is more palatable. But we need to quantify migration cost and downtime. Any rough numbers?
[04:31] Diego Ruiz: Migration from hosted to dedicated we typically support with model‑pinning and identical API surface; downtime is minimal if KV caching warmup is planned. Expect a short warmup window (minutes to an hour depending on sequence lengths and prefix cache).
[04:46] Arjun Patel: For cost comparisons, we'll return cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated reserved capacity (4xA100) vs private (op‑ex heavy initially). We'll include projected unit cost with your workload.
[04:59] Priya Shah: Also, we need audit log retention — do you have 12+ months retention options?
[05:03] Diego Ruiz: Yes, that's an add‑on for both hosted and dedicated S3 log export; private is customer managed so retention is your policy.
[05:12] Kenji Tanaka: On benchmarks: can Redwood run both throughput (sustained tokens/sec) and cold/warm path p99 tests? We want to see both steady state and cold start behavior.
[05:21] Arjun Patel: Absolutely. Plan is: 24hr sustained throughput run (to identify burn rate and cost), then a series of cold starts to measure warmup penalties, and an eval run for quality on the labeled set.
[05:33] [05:33] Sarah Conway: For quality, which model families would you test? We prefer open models that Redwood supports but also need a path to higher‑quality variants if accuracy lags.
[05:42] Maya Chen: We'll start with the curated open family you prefer (we'll propose two model variants) and include a higher‑capacity variant if you need a quality fallback. Redwood Optimize will also suggest quantization and batching settings to keep cost down while maintaining the F1 target.
[05:58] Omar Haddad: Any blockers from our side besides sample data and keys?
[06:02] Priya Shah: We'll need to review the SOW for KMS integration specifics and an architecture/network diagram. Also a simple threat model for the hosted variant.
[06:12] Maya Chen: We'll include those items in the SOW and security pack.
[06:15] [06:15] Speaker 3: (phone) sorry late join
[06:18] Arjun Patel: No problem — quick recap of the bench metrics: p99 latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, cost per 1M tokens, and accuracy F1 on the eval set. We'll attach a spreadsheet with the formulas.
[06:31] Kenji Tanaka: For acceptance, if hosted meets latency and accuracy and security can accept envelope encryption, we'd likely approve staying hosted for pilot. If not, move to dedicated. Private is last resort due to build time.
[06:47] Sarah Conway: That matches our intuition. Let's assume hosted first unless security objects after the SOC2 and KMS confirm.
[06:55] Maya Chen: Great. I'll run through a tentative timeline: today kickoff; by 2026‑07‑01 Acme provides samples; 2026‑07‑02 Redwood sends SOW + pricing; 2026‑07‑03 bench starts; 48hr bench completes by 2026‑07‑05; follow‑up 2026‑07‑07 to review. Does that fit?
[07:20] Omar Haddad: That works for us.
[07:22] Priya Shah: Yes but security will need 48 hrs to review the pack once sent.
[07:26] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll mark that. Anything else?
[07:29] Sarah Conway: One nit — please include an estimate of the engineering touch hours for private deployment. We need to budget internal ops time.
[07:36] Diego Ruiz: We'll include an estimated runbook and the ops hours for an on‑prem/private install (we typically estimate X engineer days; I'll give you a tailored number after we see the sample doc sizes).
[07:49] [07:49] Speaker 4: (end of call)

Recap (auto):
- Pilot success criteria: p99 < 800ms (512 tokens), F1 > 0.82, security/KMS + audit logs
- Bench plan: 48hr sustained + cold/warm start tests + quality eval on labeled set
- Data needed: 50 sample docs, 200 eval Q/A pairs
- Decision heuristic: hosted if meets criteria and KMS envelope acceptable; dedicated for predictable throughput and cost; private for strict data control

Explicit next steps and owners listed in action_items.

References shared in chat: SOW template (link: https://redwood.example/sow-template), benchmark spreadsheet placeholder (link: https://redwood.example/bench-template), SOC2 summary (link: https://redwood.example/security/soc2-summary).

End of transcript.
